question.text: In reviewing past performance track records in a DDQ, the data an institutional LP will typically demand includes BOTH portfolio-level IRR and investor-level IRR. The DIFFERENCE between these two is:

answer.text: Portfolio-level IRR includes taxes; investor-level IRR excludes taxes.

Portfolio-level IRR is gross AND net of all fees/expenses/carry at the fund deal portfolio level, while investor-level IRR (post fee and carry) is computed based on actual drawdowns and distributions to the investors.
Portfolio-level IRR is for listed investments only; investor-level IRR is for unlisted.
They are identical in all fund structures.

explanation.text: The Logic: Annexure 12.1 requires both: 'Portfolio level IRR, both gross and net (post all fees, expenses and carry)' and 'Investor level IRR (post fee and carry) - based on drawdowns and distribution to the investors'. The investor-level uses actual cash-flow timing (which differs from portfolio-level due to uncalled capital). The Trap: A, C, D are fabricated distinctions. Cross-Exam Context: IRR concepts also in XXI-B (PM) and XV (RA valuation), but the 'capital-call IRR vs portfolio IRR' distinction is AIF-specific due to the commitment-and-drawdown structure. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always present DPI + TVPI + IRR together — and add 'PME vs Nifty' (Public Market Equivalent). LPs who run PME analysis internally will appreciate being handed the number directly.
